 Singapore-flagged cargo ship strikes US bridge 
 Sam Chambers November 13, 2026 0 3,156 1 minute read 
 A Singapore-flagged cargoship has struck a bridge spanning the Delaware River between Philadelphia and New Jersey, forcing its closure and renewing concerns about the vulnerability of American bridges to vessel collisions.
 The 180 m Strategic Alliance, a handysize bulk carrier built in 2013, hit the Tacony-Palmyra Bridge at approximately 1.15pm local time on Thursday while its draw span was open for marine traffic. The impact damaged part of the bridge and initially prevented the structure from closing, causing extensive traffic delays on both sides of the river. No injuries were reported.
 The vessel subsequently moored at a Kinder Morgan terminal in Bristol, Pennsylvania, where US Coast Guard inspectors attended.
 The bridge, which opened in 1929 and carries up to 76,200 vehicles daily, reopened around 8.40pm, with one lane remaining closed for repairs. The cause of the collision remains under investigation.
 The incident comes as American authorities seek to strengthen protection for bridges following the March 2024 Dali disaster in Baltimore, when a containership, also Singapore-flagged, struck the Francis Scott Key Bridge, causing its collapse and killing six construction workers.
 In September, the US Coast Guard published a major review examining bridge and port infrastructure vulnerabilities across 11 ports, producing 20 recommendations for improving maritime risk management.
 Maryland is also pursuing a $177m programme to strengthen the Chesapeake Bay Bridge against ship strikes, including new protective structures around its supporting piers.
 The replacement Francis Scott Key Bridge will incorporate reinforced pier foundations and collision protection systems designed to withstand impacts from large commercial vessels.
